text: Markets are now pricing in rate hikes by year-end despite slowing GDP growth of 1.5% and surprise job losses of 23,000 in July — this stagflationary mix (sticky 3.4% inflation plus weakening employment) means the Fed is boxed in and risk assets could face pressure if conditions worsen.
BE is down 17.4% and 41.8% off its high, and despite 37% revenue growth the stock is clearly not being rewarded — trim to a smaller position size you're comfortable holding through more volatility.
META at just 15.8x earnings with 22% revenue growth and excellent cash flow is one of the cheapest large-cap growth stocks you own — consider adding on this valuation.
UNH at 17.4x earnings with 12% revenue growth and the best free cash flow in your portfolio is a defensive quality name worth adding to in a slowing economy.
GOOGL at 23x earnings with 15% revenue growth and insider buying signals confidence from people who know the company best — worth adding at this reasonable price.
